NASB.1: 'Behold, My Servant, whom I uphold; My chosen one [in whom] My soul delights. I have put My Spirit upon Him; He will bring forth justice to the nations.
NASB.2: 'He will not cry out or raise [His voice], Nor make His voice heard in the street.
NASB.3: 'A bruised reed He will not break And a dimly burning wick He will not extinguish; He will faithfully bring forth justice.
NASB.4: 'He will not be disheartened or crushed Until He has established justice in the earth; And the coastlands will wait expectantly for His law.'
NASB.5: Thus says God the LORD, Who created the heavens and stretched them out, Who spread out the earth and its offspring, Who gives breath to the people on it And spirit to those who walk in it,
NASB.6: 'I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, I will also hold you by the hand and watch over you, And I will appoint you as a covenant to the people, As a light to the nations,
NASB.7: To open blind eyes, To bring out prisoners from the dungeon And those who dwell in darkness from the prison.
NASB.8: 'I am the LORD, that is My name; I will not give My glory to another, Nor My praise to graven images.
NASB.9: 'Behold, the former things have come to pass, Now I declare new things; Before they spring forth I proclaim [them] to you.'
NASB.10: Sing to the LORD a new song, [Sing] His praise from the end of the earth! You who go down to the sea, and all that is in it. You islands, and those who dwell on them.
NASB.11: Let the wilderness and its cities lift up [their voices], The settlements where Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing aloud, Let them shout for joy from the tops of the mountains.
NASB.12: Let them give glory to the LORD And declare His praise in the coastlands.
NASB.13: The LORD will go forth like a warrior, He will arouse [His] zeal like a man of war. He will utter a shout, yes, He will raise a war cry. He will prevail against His enemies.
NASB.14: 'I have kept silent for a long time, I have kept still and restrained Myself. [Now] like a woman in labor I will groan, I will both gasp and pant.
NASB.15: 'I will lay waste the mountains and hills And wither all their vegetation; I will make the rivers into coastlands And dry up the ponds.
NASB.16: 'I will lead the blind by a way they do not know, In paths they do not know I will guide them. I will make darkness into light before them And rugged places into plains. These are the things I will do, And I will not leave them undone.'
NASB.17: They will be turned back [and] be utterly put to shame, Who trust in idols, Who say to molten images, 'You are our gods.'
NASB.18: Hear, you deaf! And look, you blind, that you may see.
NASB.19: Who is blind but My servant, Or so deaf as My messenger whom I send? Who is so blind as he that is at peace [with Me], Or so blind as the servant of the LORD?
NASB.20: You have seen many things, but you do not observe [them]; [Your] ears are open, but none hears.
NASB.21: The LORD was pleased for His righteousness' sake To make the law great and glorious.
NASB.22: But this is a people plundered and despoiled; All of them are trapped in caves, Or are hidden away in prisons; They have become a prey with none to deliver [them], And a spoil, with none to say, 'Give [them] back!'
NASB.23: Who among you will give ear to this? Who will give heed and listen hereafter?
NASB.24: Who gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned, And in whose ways they were not willing to walk, And whose law they did not obey?
NASB.25: So He poured out on him the heat of His anger And the fierceness of battle; And it set him aflame all around, Yet he did not recognize [it]; And it burned him, but he paid no attention.

ESV.1: Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.
ESV.2: He will not cry aloud or lift up his voice, or make it heard in the street;
ESV.3: a bruised reed he will not break, and a faintly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice.
ESV.4: He will not grow faint or be discouraged  till he has established justice in the earth; and the coastlands wait for his law.
ESV.5: Thus says God, the LORD, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and what comes from it, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk in it:
ESV.6: “I am the LORD; I have called you  in righteousness; I will take you by the hand and keep you; I will give you as a covenant for the people, a light for the nations,
ESV.7: to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.
ESV.8: I am the LORD; that is my name; my glory I give to no other, nor my praise to carved idols.
ESV.9: Behold, the former things have come to pass, and new things I now declare; before they spring forth I tell you of them.”
ESV.10: Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that fills it, the coastlands and their inhabitants.
ESV.11: Let the desert and its cities lift up their voice, the villages that Kedar inhabits; let the habitants of Sela sing for joy, let them shout from the top of the mountains.
ESV.12: Let them give glory to the LORD, and declare his praise in the coastlands.
ESV.13: The LORD goes out like a mighty man, like a man of war he stirs up his zeal; he cries out, he shouts aloud, he shows himself mighty against his foes.
ESV.14: For a long time I have held my peace; I have kept still and restrained myself; now I will cry out like a woman in labor; I will gasp and pant.
ESV.15: I will lay waste mountains and hills, and dry up all their vegetation; I will turn the rivers into islands,  and dry up the pools.
ESV.16: And I will lead the blind in a way that they do not know, in paths that they have not known I will guide them. I will turn the darkness before them into light, the rough places into level ground. These are the things I do, and I do not forsake them.
ESV.17: They are turned back and utterly put to shame, who trust in carved idols, who say to metal images, “You are our gods.”
ESV.18: Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see!
ESV.19: Who is blind but my servant, or deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is blind as my dedicated one,  or blind as the servant of the LORD?
ESV.20: He sees many things, but does not observe them; his ears are open, but he does not hear.
ESV.21: The LORD was pleased, for his righteousness' sake, to magnify his law and make it glorious.
ESV.22: But this is a people plundered and looted; they are all of them trapped in holes and hidden in prisons; they have become plunder with none to rescue, spoil with none to say, “Restore!”
ESV.23: Who among you will give ear to this, will attend and listen for the time to come?
ESV.24: Who gave up Jacob to the looter, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned, in whose ways they would not walk, and whose law they would not obey?
ESV.25: So he poured on him the heat of his anger and the might of battle; it set him on fire all around, but he did not understand; it burned him up, but he did not take it to heart.

NKJV.1: “Behold! My Servant whom I uphold, My Elect One in whom My soul delights! I have put My Spirit upon Him; He will bring forth justice to the Gentiles.
NKJV.2: He will not cry out, nor raise His voice, Nor cause His voice to be heard in the street.
NKJV.3: A bruised reed He will not break, And smoking flax He will not quench; He will bring forth justice for truth.
NKJV.4: He will not fail nor be discouraged, Till He has established justice in the earth;  And the coastlands shall wait for His law.”
NKJV.5: Thus says God the LORD,  Who created the heavens and stretched them out, Who spread forth the earth and that which comes from it,  Who gives breath to the people on it, And spirit to those who walk on it:
NKJV.6: “I,  the LORD, have called You in righteousness, And will hold Your hand; I will keep You and give You as a covenant to the people, As a light to the Gentiles,
NKJV.7: To open blind eyes, To bring out prisoners from the prison, Those who sit in darkness from the prison house.
NKJV.8: I am the LORD, that is My name; And My glory I will not give to another, Nor My praise to carved images.
NKJV.9: Behold, the former things have come to pass, And new things I declare; Before they spring forth I tell you of them.”
NKJV.10: Sing to the LORD a new song, And His praise from the ends of the earth, You who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, You coastlands and you inhabitants of them!
NKJV.11: Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voice, The villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing, Let them shout from the top of the mountains.
NKJV.12: Let them give glory to the LORD, And declare His praise in the coastlands.
NKJV.13: The LORD shall go forth like a mighty man; He shall stir up His zeal like a man of war. He shall cry out, yes, shout aloud; He shall prevail against His enemies.
NKJV.14: “I have held My peace a long time, I have been still and restrained Myself. Now I will cry like a woman in labor, I will pant and gasp at once.
NKJV.15: I will lay waste the mountains and hills, And dry up all their vegetation; I will make the rivers coastlands, And I will dry up the pools.
NKJV.16: I will bring the blind by a way they did not know; I will lead them in paths they have not known. I will make darkness light before them, And crooked places straight. These things I will do for them, And not forsake them.
NKJV.17: They shall be turned back, They shall be greatly ashamed, Who trust in carved images, Who say to the molded images, ‘You are our gods.’
NKJV.18: “Hear, you deaf; And look, you blind, that you may see.
NKJV.19: Who is blind but My servant, Or deaf as My messenger whom I send? Who is blind as he who is perfect, And blind as the LORD’s servant?
NKJV.20: Seeing many things, but you do not observe; Opening the ears, but he does not hear.”
NKJV.21: The LORD is well pleased for His righteousness’ sake; He will exalt the law and make it honorable.
NKJV.22: But this is a people robbed and plundered; All of them are snared in holes, And they are hidden in prison houses; They are for prey, and no one delivers; For plunder, and no one says, “Restore!”
NKJV.23: Who among you will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?
NKJV.24: Who gave Jacob for plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Was it not the LORD, He against whom we have sinned?  For they would not walk in His ways, Nor were they obedient to His law.
NKJV.25: Therefore He has poured on him the fury of His anger And the strength of battle; It has set him on fire all around, Yet he did not know; And it burned him, Yet he did not take it to heart.

NLT.1:
“Look at my servant, whom I strengthen.
He is my chosen one, who pleases me.
I have put my Spirit upon him.
He will bring justice to the nations.
NLT.2:
He will not shout
or raise his voice in public.
NLT.3:
He will not crush the weakest reed
or put out a flickering candle.
He will bring justice to all who have been wronged.
NLT.4:
He will not falter or lose heart
until justice prevails throughout the earth.
Even distant lands beyond the sea will wait for his instruction. ”
NLT.5:
God, the LORD, created the heavens and stretched them out.
He created the earth and everything in it.
He gives breath to everyone,
life to everyone who walks the earth.
And it is he who says,
NLT.6:
“I, the LORD, have called you to demonstrate my righteousness.
I will take you by the hand and guard you,
and I will give you to my people, Israel,
as a symbol of my covenant with them.
And you will be a light to guide the nations.
NLT.7:
You will open the eyes of the blind.
You will free the captives from prison,
releasing those who sit in dark dungeons.
NLT.8:
“I am the LORD; that is my name!
I will not give my glory to anyone else,
nor share my praise with carved idols.
NLT.9:
Everything I prophesied has come true,
and now I will prophesy again.
I will tell you the future before it happens.”
NLT.10:
Sing a new song to the LORD!
Sing his praises from the ends of the earth!
Sing, all you who sail the seas,
all you who live in distant coastlands.
NLT.11:
Join in the chorus, you desert towns;
let the villages of Kedar rejoice!
Let the people of Sela sing for joy;
shout praises from the mountaintops!
NLT.12:
Let the whole world glorify the LORD;
let it sing his praise.
NLT.13:
The LORD will march forth like a mighty hero;
he will come out like a warrior, full of fury.
He will shout his battle cry
and crush all his enemies.
NLT.14:
He will say, “I have long been silent;
yes, I have restrained myself.
But now, like a woman in labor,
I will cry and groan and pant.
NLT.15:
I will level the mountains and hills
and blight all their greenery.
I will turn the rivers into dry land
and will dry up all the pools.
NLT.16:
I will lead blind Israel down a new path,
guiding them along an unfamiliar way.
I will brighten the darkness before them
and smooth out the road ahead of them.
Yes, I will indeed do these things;
I will not forsake them.
NLT.17:
But those who trust in idols,
who say, ‘You are our gods,’
will be turned away in shame.
NLT.18:
“Listen, you who are deaf!
Look and see, you blind!
NLT.19:
Who is as blind as my own people, my servant?
Who is as deaf as my messenger?
Who is as blind as my chosen people,
the servant of the LORD?
NLT.20:
You see and recognize what is right
but refuse to act on it.
You hear with your ears,
but you don’t really listen.”
NLT.21:
Because he is righteous,
the LORD has exalted his glorious law.
NLT.22:
But his own people have been robbed and plundered,
enslaved, imprisoned, and trapped.
They are fair game for anyone
and have no one to protect them,
no one to take them back home.
NLT.23:
Who will hear these lessons from the past
and see the ruin that awaits you in the future?
NLT.24:
Who allowed Israel to be robbed and hurt?
It was the LORD, against whom we sinned,
for the people would not walk in his path,
nor would they obey his law.
NLT.25:
Therefore, he poured out his fury on them
and destroyed them in battle.
They were enveloped in flames,
but they still refused to understand.
They were consumed by fire,
but they did not learn their lesson.

WEB.1: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights — I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.
WEB.2: He will not shout, nor raise his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street.
WEB.3: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice.
WEB.4: He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice in the earth, and the islands will wait for his law.”
WEB.5: Thus says God Yahweh, he who created the heavens and stretched them out, he who spread out the earth and that which comes out of it, he who gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk in it.
WEB.6: “I, Yahweh, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations;
WEB.7: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
WEB.8: “I am Yahweh. That is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images.
WEB.9: Behold, the former things have happened, and I declare new things. I tell you about them before they come up.”
WEB.10: Sing to Yahweh a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is therein, the islands and their inhabitants.
WEB.11: Let the wilderness and its cities raise their voices, with the villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Let them shout from the top of the mountains!
WEB.12: Let them give glory to Yahweh, and declare his praise in the islands.
WEB.13: Yahweh will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up zeal like a man of war. He will raise a war cry. Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his enemies.
WEB.14: “I have been silent a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a travailing woman. I will both gasp and pant.
WEB.15: I will destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs. I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.
WEB.16: I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know. I will lead them in paths that they don’t know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.
WEB.17: “Those who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, ‘You are our gods’ will be turned back. They will be utterly disappointed.
WEB.18: “Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.
WEB.19: Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as he who is at peace, and as blind as Yahweh’s servant?
WEB.20: You see many things, but don’t observe. His ears are open, but he doesn’t listen.
WEB.21: It pleased Yahweh, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law, and make it honorable.
WEB.22: But this is a robbed and plundered people. All of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prisons. They have become captives, and no one delivers; and a plunder, and no one says, ‘Restore them!’
WEB.23: Who is there among you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?
WEB.24: Who gave Jacob as plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Didn’t Yahweh, he against whom we have sinned? For they would not walk in his ways, and they disobeyed his law.
WEB.25: Therefore he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle; and it set him on fire all around, but he didn’t know; and it burned him, but he didn’t take it to heart.”

AMP.1:
"Behold, My Servant, whom I uphold;
My Chosen One in whom My soul delights.
I have put My Spirit upon Him;
He will bring forth justice to the nations.
AMP.2:
"He will not call out or shout aloud,
Nor make His voice heard in the street.
AMP.3:
"A broken reed He will not break [off]
And a dimly burning wick He will not extinguish [He will not harm those who are weak and suffering];
He will faithfully bring forth justice.
AMP.4:
"He will not be disheartened or crushed [in spirit];
[He will persevere] until He has established justice on the earth;
And the coastlands will wait expectantly for His law."
AMP.5:
This is what God the LORD says,
He who created the heavens and stretched them out,
Who spread out the earth and its produce,
Who gives breath to the people on it
And spirit to those who walk on it,
AMP.6:
"I am the LORD, I have called You (the Messiah) in righteousness [for a righteous purpose],
I will also take You by the hand and keep watch over You,
And I will appoint You as a covenant to the people [Israel],
As a light to the nations (Gentiles),
AMP.7:
To open the eyes of the blind,
To bring out prisoners from the dungeon
And those who sit in darkness from the prison.
AMP.8:
"I am the LORD, that is My Name;
My glory I will not give to another,
Nor My praise to carved idols.
AMP.9:
"Indeed, the former things have come to pass,
Now I declare new things;
Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you."
AMP.10:
Sing to the LORD a new song,
Sing His praise from the end of the earth!
You who go down to the sea, and all that is in it,
You islands and coastlands, and those who inhabit them [sing His praise]!
AMP.11:
Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voices,
The villages where Kedar lives.
Let the inhabitants of Sela shout for joy,
Let them shout joyfully from the tops of the mountains.
AMP.12:
Let them give glory to the LORD
And declare His praise in the islands and coastlands.
AMP.13:
The LORD will go forth like a warrior,
He will stir up His zeal like a man of war;
He will shout out, yes, He will raise a war cry.
He will prevail [mightily] against His enemies.
AMP.14:
"I [the LORD] have been silent for a long time,
I have been still and restrained Myself.
Now I will moan like a woman in labor,
I will both gasp and pant.
AMP.15:
"I will lay waste the mountains and hills
And wither all their vegetation;
I will turn the rivers into coastlands
And dry up the ponds.
AMP.16:
"I will lead the blind by a way they do not know;
I will guide them in paths that they do not know.
I will make darkness into light before them
And rugged places into plains.
These things I will do [for them],
And I will not leave them abandoned or undone."
AMP.17:
Those who trust in carved idols will be turned back,
And utterly put to shame,
Who say to cast images,
"You are our gods."
AMP.18:
Hear, you deaf!
And look, you blind, that you may see.
AMP.19:
Who is blind but My servant [Israel],
Or deaf like My messenger whom I send?
Who is blind like the one who is at peace with Me [in a covenant relationship],
Or so blind as the servant of the LORD?
AMP.20:
You have seen many things, but you do not observe them;
Your ears are open, but no one hears.
AMP.21:
The LORD was pleased for His righteousness' sake
To make the law great and prove to be glorious.
AMP.22:
But this is a people despoiled and plundered;
All of them are trapped in holes,
Or are hidden away in prisons.
They have become a prey with no one to rescue them,
And a spoil, with no one to say, "Give them back!"
AMP.23:
Who among you will listen to this?
Who will listen and pay attention in the time to come?
AMP.24:
Who gave up Jacob [the kingdom of Judah] for spoil, and [the kingdom of] Israel to the plunderers?
Was it not the LORD, He against whom we [of Judah] have sinned,
And in whose ways they [of Israel] were unwilling to walk,
And whose law and teaching they did not obey?
AMP.25:
Therefore He poured out on Israel the heat of His anger
And the fierceness of battle;
And engulfed him in fire,
Yet he did not recognize [the lesson of repentance which the Assyrian conquest was intended to teach];
It burned him, but he did not take it to heart.

MSG.1:
"Take a good look at my servant.
I'm backing him to the hilt.
He's the one I chose,
and I couldn't be more pleased with him.
I've bathed him with my Spirit, my life.
He'll set everything right among the nations.
MSG.2:
He won't call attention to what he does
with loud speeches or gaudy parades.
MSG.3:
He won't brush aside the bruised and the hurt
and he won't disregard the small and insignificant,
but he'll steadily and firmly set things right.
MSG.4:
He won't tire out and quit. He won't be stopped
until he's finished his work—to set things right on earth.
Far-flung ocean islands
wait expectantly for his teaching."
MSG.5:
God's Message,
the God who created the cosmos, stretched out the skies,
laid out the earth and all that grows from it,
Who breathes life into earth's people,
makes them alive with his own life:
MSG.6:
"I am God. I have called you to live right and well.
I have taken responsibility for you, kept you safe.
I have set you among my people to bind them to me,
and provided you as a lighthouse to the nations,
MSG.7:
To make a start at bringing people into the open, into light:
opening blind eyes,
releasing prisoners from dungeons,
emptying the dark prisons.
MSG.8:
I am God. That's my name.
I don't franchise my glory,
don't endorse the no-god idols.
MSG.9:
Take note: The earlier predictions of judgment have been fulfilled.
I'm announcing the new salvation work.
Before it bursts on the scene,
I'm telling you all about it."
MSG.10:
Sing to God a brand-new song,
sing his praises all over the world!
Let the sea and its fish give a round of applause,
with all the far-flung islands joining in.
MSG.11:
Let the desert and its camps raise a tune,
calling the Kedar nomads to join in.
Let the villagers in Sela round up a choir
and perform from the tops of the mountains.
MSG.12:
Make God's glory resound;
echo his praises from coast to coast.
MSG.13:
God steps out like he means business.
You can see he's primed for action.
He shouts, announcing his arrival;
he takes charge and his enemies fall into line:
MSG.14:
"I've been quiet long enough.
I've held back, biting my tongue.
But now I'm letting loose, letting go,
like a woman who's having a baby—
MSG.15:
Stripping the hills bare,
withering the wildflowers,
Drying up the rivers,
turning lakes into mudflats.
MSG.16:
But I'll take the hand of those who don't know the way,
who can't see where they're going.
I'll be a personal guide to them,
directing them through unknown country.
I'll be right there to show them what roads to take,
make sure they don't fall into the ditch.
These are the things I'll be doing for them—
sticking with them, not leaving them for a minute."
MSG.17:
But those who invested in the no-gods
are bankrupt—dead broke.
MSG.18:
Pay attention! Are you deaf?
Open your eyes! Are you blind?
MSG.19:
You're my servant, and you're not looking!
You're my messenger, and you're not listening!
The very people I depended upon, servants of God,
blind as a bat—willfully blind!
MSG.20:
You've seen a lot, but looked at nothing.
You've heard everything, but listened to nothing.
MSG.21:
God intended, out of the goodness of his heart,
to be lavish in his revelation.
MSG.22:
But this is a people battered and cowed,
shut up in attics and closets,
Victims licking their wounds,
feeling ignored, abandoned.
MSG.23:
But is anyone out there listening?
Is anyone paying attention to what's coming?
MSG.24:
Who do you think turned Jacob over to the thugs,
let loose the robbers on Israel?
Wasn't it God himself, this God against whom we've sinned—
not doing what he commanded,
not listening to what he said?
MSG.25:
Isn't it God's anger that's behind all this,
God's punishing power?
Their whole world collapsed but they still didn't get it;
their life is in ruins but they don't take it to heart.

NET.1: “Here is my servant whom I support, my chosen one in whom I take pleasure. I have placed my spirit on him; he will make just decrees for the nations.
NET.2: He will not cry out or shout; he will not publicize himself in the streets.
NET.3: A crushed reed he will not break, a dim wick he will not extinguish; he will faithfully make just decrees.
NET.4: He will not grow dim or be crushed before establishing justice on the earth; the coastlands will wait in anticipation for his decrees.”
NET.5: This is what the true God, the LORD, says — the one who created the sky and stretched it out, the one who fashioned the earth and everything that lives on it, the one who gives breath to the people on it, and life to those who live on it:
NET.6: “I, the LORD, officially commission you; I take hold of your hand. I protect you and make you a covenant mediator for people, and a light to the nations,
NET.7: to open blind eyes, to release prisoners from dungeons, those who live in darkness from prisons.
NET.8: I am the LORD! That is my name! I will not share my glory with anyone else, or the praise due me with idols.
NET.9: Look, my earlier predictive oracles have come to pass; now I announce new events. Before they begin to occur, I reveal them to you.”
NET.10: Sing to the LORD a brand new song! Praise him from the horizon of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and everything that lives in it, you coastlands and those who live there!
NET.11: Let the desert and its cities shout out, the towns where the nomads of Kedar live! Let the residents of Sela shout joyfully; let them shout loudly from the mountaintops.
NET.12: Let them give the LORD the honor he deserves; let them praise his deeds in the coastlands.
NET.13: The LORD emerges like a hero, like a warrior he inspires himself for battle; he shouts, yes, he yells, he shows his enemies his power.
NET.14: “I have been inactive for a long time; I kept quiet and held back. Like a woman in labor I groan; I pant and gasp.
NET.15: I will make the trees on the mountains and hills wither up; I will dry up all their vegetation. I will turn streams into islands, and dry up pools of water.
NET.16: I will lead the blind along an unfamiliar way; I will guide them down paths they have never traveled. I will turn the darkness in front of them into light, and level out the rough ground. This is what I will do for them. I will not abandon them.
NET.17: Those who trust in idols will turn back and be utterly humiliated, those who say to metal images, ‘You are our gods.’”
NET.18: “Listen, you deaf ones! Take notice, you blind ones!
NET.19: My servant is truly blind, my messenger is truly deaf. My covenant partner, the servant of the LORD, is truly blind.
NET.20: You see many things, but don’t comprehend; their ears are open, but do not hear.”
NET.21: The LORD wanted to exhibit his justice by magnifying his law and displaying it.
NET.22: But these people are looted and plundered; all of them are trapped in pits and held captive in prisons. They were carried away as loot with no one to rescue them; they were carried away as plunder, and no one says, “Bring that back!”
NET.23: Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen attentively in the future?
NET.24: Who handed Jacob over to the robber? Who handed Israel over to the looters? Was it not the LORD, against whom we sinned? They refused to follow his commands; they disobeyed his law.
NET.25: So he poured out his fierce anger on them, along with the devastation of war. Its flames encircled them, but they did not realize it; it burned against them, but they did notice.
